ai.description: This 4–5 cm frog is brown with a distinct dark temporal streak. It features a narrow, pointed snout and a prominent dorsolateral fold. Its belly is white, and the skin is smooth.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Hylarana chitwanensis* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous white or cream-colored supralabial stripe that extends clearly to the shoulder.
ai.habitat: *Hylarana chitwanensis* inhabits subtropical moist forests and marshy areas in the Himalayan foothills, typically found near streams at altitudes below 500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Chitwan frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small invertebrates near forest streams and seasonal pools.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hylarana chitwanensis* is an oviparous frog that breeds during the monsoon season (June–August), laying clutches of small, pigmented eggs in stagnant water bodies.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Hylarana chitwanensis* is found in the Himalayan foothills of Nepal and northern India (Uttarakhand and West Bengal) at elevations between 150 and 800 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Chitwan Frog produces a series of rapid, pulsed "chirp" notes with a high pitch, typically heard from vegetation near stagnant pools or slow-moving streams.
